summary: Mitski Miyawaki is a Japanese American songwriter whose compact, emotionally direct songs swing between fuzzed-out guitar rock and theatrical art pop. She became one of the defining indie voices of the 2010s.
know: She made her first two albums as student projects while studying composition at SUNY Purchase.
Bury Me at Makeout Creek and later records were made with her longtime producer Patrick Hyland.
"My Love Mine All Mine" from 2023 became her first song to reach the Billboard Hot 100.
keyAlbums: The Land Is Inhospitable and So Are We

influencedBy.why: The sudden quiet-to-loud guitar surges on songs like "Your Best American Girl" follow the Pixies dynamic.
Her raw, confessional guitar songs with a theatrical edge sit in the line PJ Harvey opened.
Her later art-pop records share Kate Bush's mix of drama, character and unusual song structure.

influenced.why: Michelle Zauner's project toured with Mitski and works in the same Asian American indie rock lane she helped widen.
Snail Mail's diaristic guitar songs belong to the wave of young indie writers that followed Mitski's breakthrough.
Beabadoobee's mix of fuzzy guitars and bare emotional lyrics follows the path Mitski's records cleared.

cousins.why: Both write precise, intense songs about loneliness and self-image that reached far beyond their scenes.
Same generation of quietly devastating songwriters, told through folk instead of guitar rock.
Same taste for theatrical, character-driven pop that feels private and grand at once.

summary: Alvvays are a Canadian band led by Molly Rankin whose bright melodies sit inside hazy, reverb-soaked guitars. Their records updated 80s and 90s indie pop for a new generation.
know: Singer Molly Rankin grew up on Cape Breton Island in a family of well-known Celtic musicians.
Their 2014 single "Archie, Marry Me" broke them internationally.
Blue Rev was produced with Shawn Everett and largely tracked in long, continuous live takes.

influencedBy.why: The band has named Teenage Fanclub's sweet guitar pop as a touchstone for their melodies.
Their pairing of sugary tunes with fuzz and noise comes straight from the Mary Chain template.
The blurred, wavering guitar textures on Blue Rev draw on shoegaze as My Bloody Valentine defined it.
Their chiming, jangling guitar lines follow the bright jangle pop the Smiths made famous.
The dreamy reverb wash around Rankin's voice belongs to Slowdive's lineage.

cousins.why: Same big, romantic girl-group melody buried in a wall of reverb.
Both write warm, slightly melancholy melodies dressed in lush, vintage-sounding production.
Same gift for bittersweet hooks that sound happy until you listen closely.

summary: Venom were a Newcastle trio who played crude, fast, deliberately rough heavy metal with occult imagery. Their 1982 album Black Metal named an entire genre, and their speed fed thrash.
know: The classic lineup was Cronos on bass and vocals, Mantas on guitar and Abaddon on drums.
Their second album, Black Metal (1982), gave the black metal genre its name.
Their raw, distorted recordings were a deliberate rejection of polished metal production.

influencedBy.why: Venom took Motorhead's loud, fast, distorted bass-led attack and pushed it further.
Sabbath's dark, occult-themed heavy riffing is the root of Venom's image and sound.
The leather, studs and twin-guitar metal of Judas Priest shaped their look and music.
The band has cited Kiss as a model for their stage theatrics and pyrotechnics.
Their sloppy, anti-polish energy owes a lot to the British punk explosion.

influenced.why: Metallica played early shows supporting Venom and absorbed their speed and aggression.
Slayer's satanic imagery and raw speed on their early records drew on Venom.
Quorthon's first Bathory records built directly on Venom's crude, occult sound.
Mayhem named themselves after the Venom song "Mayhem with Mercy".
Tom G. Warrior's earlier band Hellhammer was built on Venom worship, and Celtic Frost grew from it.
German thrash bands like Kreator have credited Venom's speed and filth as a starting point.
The Cavalera brothers named Venom among the bands that got them started.
Darkthrone's raw black metal follows the lineage Venom started and named.

cousins.why: Same horror-movie theatrics wrapped around fast, simple, loud songs.
Both made rough, gleefully macabre British rock that scandalized its moment.

summary: Saxon are a working-class Yorkshire band who became one of the leading acts of the New Wave of British Heavy Metal. Their galloping, biker-friendly anthems were a template for 80s metal.
know: Singer Biff Byford has fronted the band since it formed out of the group Son of a Bitch.
A support slot on Motorhead's 1979 Bomber tour helped them break through.
They played the first Monsters of Rock festival at Castle Donington in 1980.

influencedBy.why: Saxon's driving riffs and Byford's high vocals follow the Deep Purple hard rock model.
Touring with Motorhead in 1979 gave Saxon their audience and toughened their sound.
Priest's twin-guitar British metal was the main model for the NWOBHM bands, Saxon included.
Their heavy blues-rock roots trace to Led Zeppelin.

influenced.why: Lars Ulrich's NWOBHM obsession included Saxon, whose riffing fed early Metallica.

cousins.why: Same plain, hard-driving rock anthems for working people.
Both made tough, melodic British Isles hard rock that bridged 70s rock and 80s metal.

summary: Def Leppard started in the New Wave of British Heavy Metal and, with producer Mutt Lange, turned into one of the biggest pop-rock bands of the 80s. Their layered vocals and glossy production set the sound of arena rock in that decade.
know: Mutt Lange produced High 'n' Dry, Pyromania and Hysteria, building their huge stacked-harmony sound.
Drummer Rick Allen plays a custom hybrid electronic and acoustic kit.
Hysteria spun off seven US singles and sold tens of millions of copies.

influencedBy.why: Lange produced their breakthrough records and shaped their polished, layered sound.
Joe Elliott has called T. Rex and glam rock his first musical love.
Elliott is an open Mott the Hoople fan and has worked on their reissues.
Bowie's glam era is a stated influence on the band's style and songwriting.
Their towering multi-tracked vocal harmonies follow Queen's approach.
The big glam choruses of the Sweet are a clear model for their hooks.
Their twin-guitar melodies draw on Thin Lizzy.

influenced.why: Bon Jovi's glossy pop-metal hits followed the radio-friendly model Pyromania set.
Taylor Swift is a longtime fan and performed with the band on CMT Crossroads in 2008.

cousins.why: Same 80s British polish and MTV-era reach, from the synth-pop side.
Both built huge, glossy 80s records with studio perfectionism.

summary: Diamond Head were a New Wave of British Heavy Metal band whose long, riff-packed songs never made them stars but shaped thrash metal. Metallica's covers of their songs made them famous to a later generation.
know: Their 1980 debut Lightning to the Nations was self-released in a plain white sleeve, earning the nickname the White Album.
Guitarist Brian Tatler and singer Sean Harris wrote the core of their catalog.
Metallica have recorded versions of "Am I Evil?", "Helpless", "The Prince" and "It's Electric".

influencedBy.why: Sean Harris's vocals and the band's long, shifting riff songs are modeled on Led Zeppelin.
Their heavy, down-stroked riffs come from the Black Sabbath tradition.
Their hard rock structures and guitar heroics draw on Deep Purple.
Priest's metal was the template for the whole NWOBHM wave Diamond Head came out of.

influenced.why: Metallica covered four Diamond Head songs and built their early riffing on Brian Tatler's style.
Dave Mustaine played Diamond Head songs in early Metallica and carried that riff-heavy approach into Megadeth.

cousins.why: Same melodic British Isles hard rock with long guitar-driven songs.
Both wrote smart, dark, riff-heavy hard rock that musicians loved more than the charts did.

summary: Dio was the band Ronnie James Dio formed after his runs with Rainbow and Black Sabbath. Its fantasy-themed anthems and his operatic voice made it a staple of 80s heavy metal.
know: Ronnie James Dio had already sung for Rainbow and Black Sabbath before launching the band.
Dio is credited with popularizing the raised horns hand sign at metal shows.
Original guitarist Vivian Campbell later joined Def Leppard.

influencedBy.why: Dio sang on Black Sabbath's Heaven and Hell and Mob Rules before starting his own band.
He fronted Rainbow with Deep Purple guitarist Ritchie Blackmore, which shaped his epic hard rock style.
His soaring, mythic vocal approach grew from the 70s hard rock that Led Zeppelin led.

influenced.why: Candlemass built epic doom on the grand, operatic metal of Dio's Sabbath and solo work.
Killswitch Engage recorded a well-known cover of "Holy Diver".
Maiden's mythic, galloping epics share and drew on the fantasy metal Dio had sung since Rainbow.

cousins.why: Same operatic vocals and grand, theatrical rock staging.
Both paired virtuoso playing with fantasy and sci-fi storytelling.

summary: Anthrax are the New York member of thrash metal's Big Four, known for mixing speed metal with hardcore punk and, unusually, hip-hop. Their 1991 "Bring the Noise" with Public Enemy was a landmark rap-metal crossover.
know: Guitarist Scott Ian and drummer Charlie Benante have been the band's core for decades.
They are counted with Metallica, Slayer and Megadeth as thrash's Big Four.
Scott Ian and Benante also made the crossover side project S.O.D. in 1985.

influencedBy.why: Their melodic speed and galloping riffs draw on Iron Maiden.
Priest's twin-guitar metal was a core early influence.
Motorhead's speed and punk attitude fed their thrash.
Scott Ian and Charlie Benante have long cited Kiss as the band that got them into rock.
The New York hardcore scene, Agnostic Front included, shaped their crossover sound.
They teamed up with Public Enemy on "Bring the Noise" and toured together.
Sabbath's heavy riffing underlies the whole thrash style.

influenced.why: Anthrax's rap-metal crossover helped clear the path for bands fusing hip-hop and heavy guitars.
Their early mix of metal and hip-hop is part of the background nu metal grew from.

cousins.why: Same New York mix of hip-hop, hardcore punk and a sense of humor.
Both broke down the wall between rap and loud rock guitars.

summary: Exodus were one of the first Bay Area thrash bands and a key part of the scene that produced Metallica and Testament. Their debut Bonded by Blood is a cornerstone of the style.
know: Kirk Hammett co-founded the band before leaving to join Metallica in 1983.
Guitarist Gary Holt is the band's main songwriter and also played in Slayer from 2011.
Bonded by Blood was recorded in 1984 but delayed until 1985.

influencedBy.why: Their twin-guitar attack grows from Judas Priest.
NWOBHM bands like Iron Maiden shaped their fast, melodic riffing.
Motorhead's speed and aggression pushed them toward thrash.
The riff-heavy NWOBHM of Diamond Head was part of the Bay Area thrash diet.
Venom's crude speed metal fed the early Bay Area scene.

influenced.why: Kirk Hammett brought his Exodus playing into Metallica when he joined in 1983.
Gary Holt joined Slayer and played on their final album and tours.
Singer Steve Souza moved from Testament's earlier lineup to Exodus, and the two bands grew up side by side.
Sepultura's thrash era drew on the Bay Area sound Exodus helped create.

cousins.why: Same raw, high-speed West Coast underground aggression from the punk side.
Bay Area peers who made fast, sharp, scene-defining music in the same years.

summary: Testament were a leading second-wave Bay Area thrash band, known for strong songwriting and Alex Skolnick's melodic lead guitar. They stayed productive long after thrash's first peak.
know: The band started under the name Legacy before switching to Testament for their 1987 debut.
Chuck Billy has been the lead singer since 1986.
Guitarist Alex Skolnick also leads a jazz trio, and drummer Dave Lombardo played on The Gathering.

influencedBy.why: They came up in the same Bay Area scene and shared singer Steve Souza in their early years.
Metallica's early albums set the template for Bay Area thrash.
Their melodic twin-guitar work draws on Iron Maiden.
Judas Priest's twin-guitar metal is a root of their style.
Former Slayer drummer Dave Lombardo played on The Gathering.

cousins.why: Same melodic, harmonized twin lead guitars.
Both are guitar-hero bands where the solos are as important as the riffs.

summary: Kreator are the leading German thrash band, led by Mille Petrozza. Their fierce mid-80s records helped define Teutonic thrash and pushed metal toward death metal.
know: Frontman Mille Petrozza has led the band since it started as Tyrant and then Tormentor.
Pleasure to Kill (1986) is often cited as a bridge between thrash and early death metal.
In the late 90s they experimented with gothic and industrial textures on Endorama.

influencedBy.why: Petrozza has named Venom as a key early influence on the band's speed and rawness.
Slayer's speed and darkness shaped Kreator's mid-80s albums.
Motorhead's punk-fueled metal was a starting point for German thrash.
Classic British metal like Judas Priest underlies their riffing.

influenced.why: Pleasure to Kill was part of the extreme thrash that early death metal like Death grew out of.
Sepultura's early thrash leaned on the German style Kreator led.

cousins.why: Same relentless, furious energy from the hardcore punk side.
Both paired fast, aggressive music with pointed political lyrics.

summary: Sepultura rose from Brazil to become one of the most important metal bands of the 90s. They moved from raw thrash to heavy groove and, on Roots, folded in Brazilian percussion and indigenous music.
know: Brothers Max and Igor Cavalera founded the band as teenagers.
Roots (1996) was produced by Ross Robinson and includes recordings made with the Xavante people.
After Max left in 1996, Derrick Green became singer in 1998.

influencedBy.why: The Cavaleras have named Venom as one of the bands that started them.
Slayer's speed and darkness shaped their early thrash.
German thrash like Kreator was a major early model.
Max Cavalera has often named Celtic Frost as a core influence.
Motorhead's raw attack fed their early sound.
Korn's Jonathan Davis guested on Roots, which also shared Korn's producer Ross Robinson.
Mike Patton guested on Roots alongside Jonathan Davis.

influenced.why: Slipknot's tribal percussion and groove owe a lot to Roots, made with their future producer Ross Robinson.
Joe Duplantier of Gojira later played with Max and Igor in Cavalera Conspiracy and has cited the band.
Deftones toured with Sepultura and absorbed their groove-heavy 90s sound.

cousins.why: Fellow Brazilians who took a foreign rock style and made it unmistakably Brazilian.
Same furious, political, rhythm-first protest music.

summary: Celtic Frost grew out of Hellhammer and made some of the most influential extreme metal of the 80s. They mixed crushing, primitive riffs with gothic and orchestral ideas.
know: Tom G. Warrior and Martin Eric Ain formed the band from the ashes of Hellhammer in 1984.
Into the Pandemonium (1987) added orchestral parts, female vocals and a cover of Wall of Voodoo.
They returned in 2006 with the slow, heavy Monotheist.

influencedBy.why: Hellhammer, the band before Celtic Frost, was openly modeled on Venom.
Their slow, heavy riffing comes straight from Black Sabbath.
Motorhead's raw speed shaped Hellhammer and early Celtic Frost.
Their gothic turn on Into the Pandemonium reflects the dark post-punk Tom G. Warrior loved.

influenced.why: Early Norwegian black metal, Mayhem included, drew heavily on Hellhammer and Celtic Frost.
Fenriz of Darkthrone has repeatedly named Celtic Frost as a central influence.
Max Cavalera has called Celtic Frost one of his main influences.
Their primitive, heavy extreme metal fed the early death metal sound.
Mikael Akerfeldt has named Celtic Frost among his formative extreme metal bands.
Morbid Angel's dark, heavy approach drew on Celtic Frost.

cousins.why: Same dark, gothic gloom with dramatic, ritual-like intensity.
Both made abrasive, primal, menacing music that defied its scene's rules.

summary: Bathory was essentially the solo project of Quorthon, who helped define first-wave black metal and then invented viking metal. His raw early records and later Norse epics were hugely influential in Scandinavia.
know: Quorthon wrote the songs and played most of the instruments himself.
Bathory never played a proper live concert.
Blood Fire Death and Hammerheart introduced the slow, epic Norse style later called viking metal.
keyAlbums: Under the Sign of the Black Mark

influencedBy.why: Bathory's first records drew directly on Venom's raw, occult metal.
Quorthon's early speed and distortion come from Motorhead.
Sabbath's dark heaviness underpins his slower epic material.

influenced.why: Bathory's raw sound was a major model for Mayhem and Norwegian black metal.
Darkthrone's cold, raw black metal draws on early Bathory.
Emperor have named Bathory as a key influence on their atmosphere.
Burzum's early records follow Bathory's lo-fi, atmospheric black metal.

cousins.why: Same ancient, epic, myth-heavy atmosphere.
Both built huge, cinematic soundscapes from a largely solo studio approach.

summary: Death was Chuck Schuldiner's band and one of the founders of death metal. Over seven albums he moved from raw gore-themed metal to complex, melodic and progressive music.
know: Chuck Schuldiner was the only constant member and is often called the father of death metal.
Human (1991) featured Paul Masvidal and Sean Reinert of Cynic and marked a turn toward technical playing.
Drummer Gene Hoglan played on Individual Thought Patterns and Symbolic.

influencedBy.why: Schuldiner named Venom among the extreme bands that shaped his early sound.
Slayer's speed and darkness helped push Death beyond thrash.
German thrash like Kreator fed his early sound.
Celtic Frost's heavy extremity was part of the early death metal blueprint.
Schuldiner loved Iron Maiden, and their melody shows in Death's later work.

influenced.why: Cannibal Corpse built on the Florida death metal sound Death helped create.
Swedish melodic death metal drew on Death's melodic later records.
Mikael Akerfeldt has named Death as an influence on combining extremity and melody.
Gojira have cited Death as a formative band.
The two bands grew up together in Florida and shaped each other's scene.

cousins.why: Same drive toward musicianship and complexity inside heavy music.
Both kept reinventing their sound around one restless guitarist-leader.

summary: Morbid Angel are one of the founding Florida death metal bands, built around Trey Azagthoth's otherworldly guitar and blinding speed. Their early albums are among the most respected in the genre.
know: Their first albums were released in alphabetical order: Altars, Blessed, Covenant, Domination and so on.
Covenant (1993) came out through a major-label deal with Giant Records, rare for death metal then.
Drummer Pete Sandoval's blast beats set a new speed standard.

influencedBy.why: Slayer's speed and chromatic riffing are a clear root of Morbid Angel's sound.
Celtic Frost's dark heaviness fed their slower, crushing passages.
Venom's occult extremity was part of the band's starting point.
German thrash like Kreator helped push them toward death metal speed.

influenced.why: Joe Duplantier has named Morbid Angel as one of Gojira's biggest influences.
Cannibal Corpse moved to Tampa and became part of the scene Morbid Angel anchored.
Morbid Angel's low, heavy riffing is part of the extreme metal background Meshuggah grew from.

cousins.why: Same wild, otherworldly lead guitar that bends sound into new shapes.
Both built a whole cosmic mythology around their music.

summary: Cannibal Corpse are the best-selling death metal band in the US and one of the genre's most consistent. They formed in Buffalo and became a fixture of the Tampa scene.
know: Bassist Alex Webster is a founding member and a widely admired technical player.
George "Corpsegrinder" Fisher replaced original singer Chris Barnes in 1995.
The band made a cameo in the 1994 film Ace Ventura: Pet Detective.

influencedBy.why: Slayer's speed and aggression underlie their style.
Death's early Florida records set the template they followed.
They joined the Tampa scene that Morbid Angel helped build.
German thrash like Kreator fed their early sound.

cousins.why: Same love of horror-movie imagery played straight and loud.
Both turned horror theater into a long-running musical career.

summary: Napalm Death created grindcore, fusing hardcore punk speed with extreme metal heaviness into very short, very fast songs. Their debut Scum is the genre's founding record.
know: "You Suffer" is listed by Guinness as the shortest recorded song, at about one second.
BBC DJ John Peel championed them with radio sessions in the late 80s.
Early members included Justin Broadrick, later of Godflesh, and Lee Dorrian, later of Cathedral.

influencedBy.why: They grew from anarcho and hardcore punk and have long covered a Dead Kennedys song live.
American hardcore like Black Flag fed their speed and intensity.
Celtic Frost's heaviness pushed them from punk toward extreme metal.
Bad Brains' blistering hardcore speed is part of grindcore's DNA.

influenced.why: Bill Steer played guitar in Napalm Death before focusing on Carcass, which began as a grindcore band in their mold.
Converge's fusion of hardcore and extreme metal draws on the grindcore Napalm Death invented.
Dillinger's blasts and chaos come partly from grindcore.

cousins.why: Same short, fast, ethically charged punk songs.
Both kept a fiercely independent, politically engaged stance for decades.

summary: Carcass began as pioneers of goregrind and then, with Heartwork, helped create melodic death metal. Few bands changed shape so much and stayed this influential.
know: Guitarist Bill Steer also played in Napalm Death in the late 80s.
Their early lyrics were written in deliberately clinical medical vocabulary.
Guitarist Michael Amott later formed Arch Enemy.
songs: Keep On Rotting in the Free World

influencedBy.why: Bill Steer played in Napalm Death, and early Carcass grew from the same grindcore.
Slayer's extreme thrash shaped their riffing.
The twin-guitar melodies of Heartwork draw on classic British metal like Judas Priest.
Their melodic leads point back to Iron Maiden.
Celtic Frost's heaviness was part of their early extreme metal palette.

influenced.why: Heartwork's melodic death metal was a direct model for the Gothenburg sound.
In Flames built on the melodic extreme metal Heartwork mapped out.
Metalcore's melodic riffing traces through Heartwork.

cousins.why: Same abrasive, clinical, provocative take on noise.
Both made harmonized twin guitar leads the heart of their sound.

summary: At the Gates were a Gothenburg band whose 1995 album Slaughter of the Soul became the blueprint for melodic death metal and a key source for American metalcore.
know: Tomas Lindberg has been the singer since the band formed.
Twin brothers Anders and Jonas Bjorler left after Slaughter of the Soul and formed The Haunted.
The band reunited in 2007 and released new albums starting with At War with Reality in 2014.
keyAlbums: The Red in the Sky Is Ours
With Fear I Kiss the Burning Darkness

influencedBy.why: Carcass's melodic turn shaped At the Gates' tight, melodic riffing.
Death's later melodic death metal informed their style.
Their harmonized guitar melodies draw on Iron Maiden.
Celtic Frost's dark extremity was part of their early sound.

influenced.why: Killswitch Engage and American metalcore took Slaughter of the Soul as a template.
Fellow Gothenburg band In Flames developed the same melodic style alongside them.
Avenged Sevenfold's early metalcore riffing drew on the Gothenburg sound.

cousins.why: Same compact, furious songwriting with a hardcore punk spine.
Both put strong melody inside loud, fast, abrasive music.

summary: In Flames were one of the creators of the Gothenburg melodic death metal sound, adding Swedish folk melodies to extreme metal. They later moved toward American alternative metal and reached a wider audience.
know: Guitarist Jesper Stromblad founded the band, and Anders Friden became singer in 1995.
Friden previously sang in Dark Tranquillity, the other key Gothenburg band.
Clayman (2000) and Reroute to Remain (2002) started their shift toward cleaner, more modern metal.

influencedBy.why: Their harmonized twin guitars come straight from Iron Maiden.
Carcass's melodic death metal helped shape their style.
They grew up alongside At the Gates in the same Gothenburg scene.
Metallica's thrash riffing is part of their foundation.
Their 2000s records drew on the American alternative metal of bands like Deftones.

influenced.why: Killswitch Engage and American metalcore leaned heavily on In Flames' melodic riffing.
Avenged Sevenfold's early metalcore drew on Gothenburg melodies.
Early metalcore bands like Bring Me the Horizon inherited the In Flames style.

cousins.why: Same melodic, harmonized twin guitar leads.
Both carry a strong Swedish gift for sweet, melancholy melody.

summary: Mayhem are the central band of the Norwegian black metal scene. Their 1994 album De Mysteriis Dom Sathanas is one of the genre's defining records.
know: The band took its name from the Venom song "Mayhem with Mercy".
Hungarian singer Attila Csihar sang on De Mysteriis Dom Sathanas and later rejoined.
Guitarist Euronymous ran the Oslo record shop Helvete and the label Deathlike Silence, hubs of the early scene.

influencedBy.why: Mayhem were named after a Venom song and built on their raw occult metal.
Bathory's cold, raw early records were a central model.
Hellhammer and Celtic Frost shaped their primitive heaviness.
Slayer's speed and darkness fed their early sound.

influenced.why: Darkthrone moved from death metal to black metal within the scene Mayhem led.
Emperor came up in the scene centered on Mayhem and Helvete.
Varg Vikernes played bass on De Mysteriis Dom Sathanas.
Mayhem singer Attila Csihar became a regular vocalist with Sunn O))).
Deafheaven's tremolo-picked black metal grows from the Norwegian sound Mayhem defined.

cousins.why: Same theatrical, gothic sense of darkness.
Both made cold, bleak, highly atmospheric music that defined a scene.

summary: Burzum is the one-man project of Varg Vikernes, whose hypnotic, lo-fi records shaped atmospheric black metal. Their repetitive, trance-like style also fed ambient and blackgaze music.
know: Vikernes recorded the albums alone, playing all instruments.
The early albums were recorded at Grieghallen studio in Bergen with producer Pytten.
He used a deliberately harsh, fuzzy guitar tone on Filosofem.

influencedBy.why: Burzum's raw atmosphere draws directly on early Bathory.
Vikernes played bass on Mayhem's De Mysteriis Dom Sathanas.
Celtic Frost's heaviness is part of the early black metal background.
Venom's raw occult metal underlies the whole style.

influenced.why: Deafheaven's long, hypnotic black metal builds draw on Burzum's repetitive style.

cousins.why: Same slow-moving, hypnotic, ambient-minded repetition.
Both built long, trance-like pieces from simple, repeating parts.

summary: Emperor were the most ambitious band of Norwegian black metal, adding orchestral keyboards and complex structures to the genre. In the Nightside Eclipse is a landmark of symphonic black metal.
know: Ihsahn and Samoth formed the band as teenagers.
Their records layered keyboards over tremolo guitars to create an orchestral sound.
Ihsahn later built a solo career in progressive metal.
keyAlbums: Anthems to the Welkin at Dusk
Prometheus: The Discipline of Fire & Demise
songs: The Loss and Curse of Reverence

influencedBy.why: Bathory's epic atmosphere is a stated influence on the band.
They came up in the Oslo-centered scene that Mayhem led.
Celtic Frost's dark ambition was a model for extreme metal with grand ideas.
Ihsahn has named Iron Maiden as his first big metal love.
Venom's black metal laid the groundwork.

influenced.why: Deafheaven's grand, layered black metal follows the ambition Emperor showed.
Opeth and Emperor both pushed extreme metal toward progressive structure, and Ihsahn and Mikael Akerfeldt are longtime peers.

cousins.why: Same grand, synthesizer-built orchestral scale.
Both brought progressive complexity into dark, heavy music.

summary: Darkthrone are a Norwegian duo whose cold, raw early 90s albums defined lo-fi black metal. Later they embraced crust punk and old-school heavy metal while refusing to tour.
know: The band has long been the duo of Fenriz and Nocturno Culto.
Their 1991 debut Soulside Journey was a death metal album before they switched to black metal.
Darkthrone has not played live in decades.
keyAlbums: A Blaze in the Northern Sky
songs: In the Shadow of the Horns

influencedBy.why: Fenriz has called Celtic Frost one of the band's most important influences.
Early Bathory's raw coldness shaped their black metal turn.
Venom's crude metal is at the root of their style.
They switched to black metal inside the scene Mayhem led.
Their later punk-metal records lean on Motorhead's raw rock.

influenced.why: Deafheaven's tremolo picking and raw passages draw on Darkthrone's style.

cousins.why: Same stubborn DIY punk spirit and raw sound.
Both made fast, raw, horror-tinged music that stayed underground on purpose.

summary: Candlemass are the Swedish band that defined epic doom metal, pairing Black Sabbath's slow heaviness with operatic vocals and grand melodies. Their debut gave the style its name.
know: Bassist Leif Edling is the band's founder and main songwriter.
Their 1986 debut was titled Epicus Doomicus Metallicus, which gave epic doom its label.
Singer Messiah Marcolin, known for performing in a monk's robe, fronted their classic late-80s albums.

influencedBy.why: Leif Edling has always named Black Sabbath as the foundation of Candlemass.
Their operatic vocals and epic scale follow the Dio-era Sabbath and Dio's own band.
Their grand melodic heavy metal draws on Iron Maiden.

influenced.why: Candlemass's epic doom was a key model for the British doom-death bands.
Ghost's slow, melodic, occult-themed heavy rock draws on Swedish doom like Candlemass.

cousins.why: Same solemn, ceremonial grandeur.
Both built slow, majestic, melancholy songs on a big scale.

summary: Saint Vitus were Los Angeles doom pioneers who played slow, heavy Sabbath-style metal while signed to a punk label. They became a cornerstone of American doom.
know: They signed to SST Records, the punk label run by Black Flag's Greg Ginn.
Scott "Wino" Weinrich of The Obsessed became their singer in 1986.
The band took its name from the Black Sabbath song "St. Vitus Dance".

influencedBy.why: They are named after a Sabbath song and built their sound on Sabbath's slow riffs.
They toured with and recorded for Black Flag's label SST, and shared their punk attitude.
Blue Cheer's loud, primitive heaviness is part of their DNA.

influenced.why: Electric Wizard's crushing doom follows the path Saint Vitus laid down.
Sleep's slow Sabbath-worship grew from the American doom tradition Vitus led.
Sludge bands like Eyehategod took Vitus's punk-meets-doom approach further.

cousins.why: Same slow, heavy riffs played with a punk attitude.

summary: Steve Albini was a Chicago musician and recording engineer who made raw, live-sounding records for Pixies, Nirvana, PJ Harvey and many others. He led Big Black and Shellac and rejected producer royalties on principle.
know: He preferred a "recorded by" credit to "produced by" and charged a flat fee rather than royalties.
He built and ran Electrical Audio, a studio in Chicago.
He led the bands Big Black and Shellac.

influencedBy.why: The Stooges' raw, loud sound is a model for his recording philosophy.
Albini has named Wire as a key influence on his playing and attitude.
Gang of Four's sharp, scratchy guitar shaped Big Black's sound.
The Birthday Party's abrasive post-punk was a touchstone.
Pere Ubu's noisy, art-damaged rock fed his aesthetic.
The Ramones were his entry point into punk.

influenced.why: Founded and led Big Black.
Recorded Surfer Rosa and shaped its loud, raw drum sound.
Recorded the Breeders' debut Pod.
Recorded In Utero, giving it a rougher sound than Nevermind.
Recorded Rid of Me, one of her rawest records.
Recorded Times of Grace and later Neurosis albums.
Recorded Sunn O)))'s Life Metal and Pyroclasts.
Recorded Slint's debut Tweez.
Recorded Mogwai's My Father My King.
Recorded Godspeed's Yanqui U.X.O.
Recorded much of Jawbreaker's 24 Hour Revenge Therapy.
Recorded the Manic Street Preachers' Journal for Plague Lovers.

cousins.why: Same stripped-back philosophy of capturing a band's raw sound.
Both prized raw, live energy over studio polish.

summary: Butch Vig is a producer and drummer who made Nirvana's Nevermind and Smashing Pumpkins' first albums, shaping the polished, powerful sound of 90s alternative rock. He also co-founded Garbage.
know: He co-founded Smart Studios in Madison, Wisconsin, with Steve Marker.
He is the drummer and a co-founder of the band Garbage.
He also produced Sonic Youth's Dirty, L7's Bricks Are Heavy and Green Day's 21st Century Breakdown.

influencedBy.why: His focus on layered, melodic pop production follows the Beatles' studio craft.
His polished, layered studio approach follows George Martin's model of producer as arranger.
Cheap Trick's heavy Midwest power pop is part of the sound he brought to grunge.

influenced.why: Produced Nevermind and gave it its huge, polished punch.
Produced Gish and Siamese Dream, building their layered guitar sound.
Produced Sonic Youth's Dirty.
Produced L7's Bricks Are Heavy.
Produced Wasting Light, recorded on analog tape in Dave Grohl's garage.
Produced 21st Century Breakdown.

cousins.why: Same polished, heavy, radio-ready production that defined a decade.
Both made loud guitar music sound huge and radio-ready.
